input: Find a mentor in the UX design field

gold.taskTitle: Find a UX Design Mentor for Career Growth
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to find and connect with a mentor who works in the UX design field.

questions.title: What is your current experience level in UX design?
questions.description: Understanding whether the user is a complete beginner, a career switcher, or a mid-level designer shapes what kind of mentor they need.

questions.title: What specific area of UX do you want guidance in?
questions.description: UX is broad — the user may want help with research, interaction design, portfolio building, or breaking into the industry.

questions.title: What is your primary goal for having a mentor?
questions.description: The user may want accountability, career advice, skill feedback, job referrals, or industry networking — each points to a different mentor profile.

questions.title: Do you prefer a mentor in a specific industry or company type?
questions.description: The user may want someone from tech, agency, healthcare, a FAANG company, or a startup, which narrows the search significantly.

questions.title: How often do you want to meet with your mentor?
questions.description: Frequency expectations — weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly — affect which platforms or people to target.

questions.title: Are you open to a paid mentorship platform or only free options?
questions.description: Some platforms like ADPList are free while others like MentorCruise involve a subscription fee — budget matters here.

questions.title: Do you have any existing network connections in UX design?
questions.description: Knowing if the user already has LinkedIn contacts, alumni, or colleagues in UX helps determine whether to start internally or from scratch.
